{"status": "NO_PLAN", "reasons": ["CS2102 requires CS2030S (completed) and (CS1231 or CS2040S etc). CS2040S is completed, so CS2102 is eligible in Sem 4. However, CS3230 requires CS2040S (completed) and CS1231S (completed). CS3219 requires CS2103T (completed). CS4238 requires CS3235. CS3235 requires CS2105, CS2106, and CS2107. The student has not completed CS2106, CS2107, or CS2105. CS2105 requires CS2040S (completed). CS2106 requires CS2100 (completed). CS2107 has no prereqs. So CS2105, CS2106, CS2107 can be taken. But CS3235 requires all three. CS4238 requires CS3235. The student wants CS3230 as early as possible. CS3230 prereqs are met. CS3219 prereqs are met. CS3219 must be before CS3230. Sem 4 is exchange (0 MC). Sem 5 is NOC (0 MC). Sem 6 is NOC (0 MC). Sem 7 is NOC (0 MC). Sem 8 is the last semester. The student must take CS2105, CS2106, CS2107, CS3235, CS4238, CS3219, CS3230, CS2102. CS2102 is fixed in Sem 4? No, Sem 4 is exchange. The student said 'CS2102 has to be in semester 4'. But Sem 4 is exchange. Exchange semesters have 0 MC. You cannot take a 4 MC module in an exchange semester. This is a contradiction. Even if we ignore the 0 MC rule for a moment, Sem 4 is Y2S2. The student is currently in Sem 4. If they are on exchange in Y3S1 (Sem 5), then Sem 4 is the current semester. But they said 'I will be away on exchange in year 3 semester 1'. This implies Sem 5 is exchange. Sem 4 is NOT exchange. Wait, 'This semester is semester 4 for me'. 'I will be away on exchange in year 3 semester 1'. Y3S1 is Sem 5. So Sem 4 is NOT exchange. The student said 'CS2102 has to be in semester 4'. This is possible. However, CS3230 requires CS3219. CS3219 requires CS2103T (done). CS3230 requires CS2040S (done) and CS1231S (done). So CS3219 and CS3230 can be taken in Sem 4? No, CS3219 must be BEFORE CS3230. So CS3219 in Sem 4, CS3230 in Sem 6? Sem 6 is NOC. NOC is 0 MC. So CS3230 cannot be in Sem 6. Sem 7 is NOC. Sem 8 is the only semester left for courses. CS3230 must be in Sem 8. CS3219 must be in Sem 4 or 5? Sem 5 is exchange (0 MC). So CS3219 must be in Sem 4. Sem 4 has CS2102 and CS3219. That's 8 MC. OK. Then CS3230 in Sem 8. Now CS4238 requires CS3235. CS3235 requires CS2105, CS2106, CS2107. CS2105 requires CS2040S (done). CS2106 requires CS2100 (done). CS2107 has no prereqs. These three can be taken in Sem 4? Sem 4 already has CS2102 and CS3219 (8 MC). Limit is 20. Can add 3 more? 8+12=20. Yes. So Sem 4: CS2102, CS3219, CS2105, CS2106, CS2107. Then CS3235 in Sem 6? Sem 6 is NOC (0 MC). Cannot take CS3235. Sem 7 is NOC (0 MC). Cannot take CS3235. Sem 8 is the only option for CS3235 and CS4238. But CS3230 is also in Sem 8. Sem 8: CS3230, CS3235, CS4238. That's 12 MC. OK. But wait, CS3235 requires CS2105, CS2106, CS2107. If these are in Sem 4, CS3235 can be in Sem 6? No, Sem 6 is NOC. Sem 7 is NOC. So CS3235 MUST be in Sem 8. And CS4238 MUST be in Sem 8. And CS3230 MUST be in Sem 8. This fits. But is there any other constraint? 'CS2102 has to be in semester 4'. Done. 'CS3219 as early as possible'. Sem 4 is earliest. 'CS3230 as early as possible'. Sem 8 is earliest because Sem 6,7 are NOC. 'CS2105 as early as possible'. Sem 4 is earliest. So the plan is: Sem 4: CS2102, CS3219, CS2105, CS2106, CS2107. Sem 8: CS3230, CS3235, CS4238. Sem 5,6,7 are NOC/Exchange. This seems valid. Why NO_PLAN? Let's re-read carefully. 'I will do NOC in semester 6. I will do NOC in semester 7.' 'I will be away on exchange in year 3 semester 1'. Y3S1 is Sem 5. So Sem 5 is Exchange. Sem 6 is NOC. Sem 7 is NOC. Sem 8 is regular. Sem 4 is regular. The student is IN Sem 4. So Sem 4 is the current semester. The plan starts from Sem 4. Sem 4: CS2102, CS3219, CS2105, CS2106, CS2107. Sem 5: Exchange (0 MC). Sem 6: NOC (0 MC). Sem 7: NOC (0 MC). Sem 8: CS3230, CS3235, CS4238. This works. Is CS3235 eligible in Sem 8? Prereqs: CS2105, CS2106, CS2107. All completed in Sem 4. Yes. Is CS4238 eligible? Prereq CS3235. Completed in Sem 8? No, CS3235 is in Sem 8. CS4238 is in Sem 8. Prerequisite must be completed OR planned in a STRICTLY earlier semester. CS3235 is in the SAME semester as CS4238. This violates Rule 4. CS4238 cannot be taken in the same semester as CS3235. CS3235 must be in an earlier semester. But Sem 5,6,7 are 0 MC. So CS3235 cannot be taken in Sem 5,6,7. Therefore, CS3235 cannot be completed before Sem 8. Therefore, CS4238 cannot be taken in Sem 8 (or later, as there is no later semester). Thus, CS4238 cannot be taken. Status NO_PLAN.

Wait, did I miss a semester? Y4S1 is Sem 7. Y4S2 is Sem 8. The student is in Sem 4. Sem 5,6,7 are blocked for MC. Sem 8 is the last. CS3235 must be before CS4238. CS3235 needs a semester with MC. Only Sem 4 and Sem 8 have MC. If CS3235 is in Sem 4, then CS4238 can be in Sem 8. Can CS3235 be in Sem 4? Prereqs: CS2105, CS2106, CS2107. If CS3235 is in Sem 4, then CS2105, CS2106, CS2107 must be in Sem 4 or earlier. They are not completed. So they must be in Sem 4. Corequisites? No, they are prerequisites. Rule 4: 'Prerequisites must be completed or planned in a STRICTLY earlier semester.' So CS2105, CS2106, CS2107 must be in Sem 3 or earlier. They are not completed. So they cannot be taken in Sem 4 if CS3235 is also in Sem 4. They must be taken in Sem 3? But the student is in Sem 4. They cannot go back. So CS2105, CS2106, CS2107 must be taken in Sem 4. Then CS3235 must be in Sem 6 or later. But Sem 6,7 are 0 MC. So CS3235 must be in Sem 8. Then CS4238 must be in Sem 10? No Sem 10. So CS4238 cannot be taken.

Therefore, NO_PLAN.

One check: Is CS2105, CS2106, CS2107 corequisites for CS3235? No, they are prerequisites. 'prerequisite: (CS2105 ...) and (CS2106 ...) and CS2107'. So they must be strictly earlier.

So, CS2105, CS2106, CS2107 must be in Sem 4 (earliest available). CS3235 must be in Sem 6 or later. Sem 6,7 are 0 MC. So CS3235 must be in Sem 8. CS4238 must be in Sem 10. Impossible.

Thus, NO_PLAN.
